lesson: Word List 8 — the last three words
cite: Wordly Wise 3000, Book 6, Word List 8, page 85
title: Word List 8 — The last three words
intro: Skirmish, supplement and territory came on page 85 and were missed when the rest of Word List 8 was built. This is the same five parts the real paper has, over those three words only — with a few of the twelve you already know mixed in, because that is how they will arrive on Friday.
rule: Five parts, 28 points — a short section, not the teacher's paper. Parts III and V are the ones nobody can tap their way through: you write the word yourself, then you write whole sentences and mark them against an answer worth full marks.

parts.name: Part I
parts.title: Vocabulary Matching
parts.how: Choose the letter of the best definition for each word.
defs: a wide, open area or surface; a stretch
a minor fight or battle; or to take part in one
a long journey by a group to explore or do battle
a particular area of land; or land under a government's control
something added to make up for what is missing; or to add to

parts.name: Part II
parts.title: Multiple Choice: Meaning in Context
parts.how: Choose the word that best completes each sentence.

items.q: Apart from a few ______, both sides kept the cease-fire that had been agreed to.
items.why: A skirmish is a minor fight or battle. The plural takes -es, because the word ends in -sh.

items.q: The two armies began to ______ in the woods a week before the major battle.
items.why: The same word as a verb: to take part in a minor fight. A battle is the big one; this is the small one.

items.q: Those who eat a well-balanced diet probably do not need vitamin ______.
items.why: A supplement is something added to make up for something missing — here, what the food leaves out.

items.q: Each summer I ______ my allowance with the money I earn from a paper route.
items.why: The same word as a verb: to add to. The noun and the verb are spelled exactly the same.

items.q: A dog will defend its ______ against any other dog that comes near the garden.
items.why: A particular area of land — the patch an animal treats as its own. An expanse is wide and open; a territory is held.

items.q: The island of Guam is a ______ of the United States.
items.why: The second meaning: a land area under the control of a particular group or government.

parts.name: Part III
parts.title: Write the Word
parts.how: Write the vocabulary word on each line. Spelling counts.

items.q: A noun meaning a minor fight or battle:
items.why: Skirmish. A battle is the big one; this is the small one that happens before or beside it.

items.q: A verb meaning to add to something that is not enough on its own:
items.why: Supplement. The noun and the verb are spelled the same — only the job in the sentence changes.

items.q: A noun meaning an area of land held by a group or a government:
items.why: Territory. Its other meaning is any particular area of land, such as the patch a dog defends.

items.q: The plural of the word for a small battle — the ending changes:
items.why: Skirmishes. A word ending in -sh takes -es, not -s.

items.q: The plural of the word for an area of land — the y changes:

parts.name: Part IV
parts.title: Parts of Speech
parts.how: Write noun, verb, adjective or adverb for the bold word as it is used.

items.q: Apart from a few skirmishes, both sides kept the cease-fire.
items.why: A noun — the fights themselves. You can count them, which is the giveaway: a few of them.

items.q: I supplement my allowance with earnings from a paper route.
items.why: A verb — it is something I do to my allowance.

items.q: The two sides began to skirmish before the major battle.
items.why: A verb. The to in front of it is the clue: began to skirmish.

items.q: The island of Guam is a territory of the United States.
items.why: A noun — the thing Guam is. Territory is only ever a noun, whichever of its two meanings is in play.

items.q: Those who eat a well-balanced diet do not need vitamin supplements.
items.why: A noun here — the things themselves, the pills in the bottle. The same word was a verb two questions ago.

parts.name: Part V
parts.title: Application & Critical Thinking
parts.how: Answer in complete sentences, using the vocabulary word correctly.

items.q: Use skirmish and territory together in one logical sentence.
items.model: The two patrols fought a brief skirmish along the edge of the disputed territory, and both sides pulled back before dark.

sense.ask: Picture it first: a small fight, and the piece of land somebody is claiming. Say who was fighting, and whose land it was.

show.why: A skirmish is a small fight. Say who was doing the fighting, or what the fight was over.
A territory is a piece of land somebody holds. Say whose it was, or where it was.

avoid.why: That tells me what the words mean instead of using them. Write a sentence where they are just doing their job.

items.q: Supplement has two jobs on this list. Use it as a verb, meaning to add to something that is not enough on its own.
items.model: My brother supplements his wages by washing cars on a Saturday morning.

sense.ask: Say what was not enough on its own, and then say what you added to it.
sense.note: Nothing here can tell the verb from the noun — "I take a vitamin supplement every morning" satisfies both groups and is the wrong job. Spotting that is his to do against the model answer, and guessing at it with a word list would cost him right answers. Do not add a group for it without running the trials in _build/test_sense.js.

show.why: To supplement is to top up something that is short. Say what was short — your allowance, your dinner, your hours of practice.
Say what you actually added — the extra job, the handful of nuts, the extra half-hour.

avoid.why: That tells me what the word means instead of using it. Write a sentence where the word is just doing its job.

items.q: Territory has two meanings. Use it in a sentence where it means land under the control of a group or a government — not just a patch of ground.
items.model: Guam is a small island in the Pacific, and it has been a territory of the United States for more than a century.

sense.ask: Name the country, the government or the group that holds the land, and say where it is.

show.why: Here a territory belongs to somebody — a country, a government, a tribe. Say who holds it.
Say where it is, or what kind of place it is — an island, a stretch of coast, a region in the north.

avoid.why: That tells me what the word means instead of using it. Write a sentence where the word is just doing its job.
